info.title: Extreme Platform ONE REST API - Device Lifecycle Management
info.description:
The Extreme Platform ONE™ Device Lifecycle Management API provides comprehensive
automation and orchestration for the complete network device lifecycle, from 
initial discovery and zero-touch onboarding through operational management 
and secure decommissioning.

**🔄 Complete Lifecycle Management:**

• **Zero-Touch Device Onboarding** - Fully automated provisioning for wireless 
devices (IQEngine/XIQ) and wired devices (EXOS/VOSS) with intelligent 
configuration validation and compliance checking

• **Intelligent Bulk Operations** - Enterprise-scale batch processing with 
Excel-based import/export, template-driven workflows, and automated 
validation for efficient mass device management

• **Advanced Device Discovery** - Device detection and classification 
with automatic product compatibility checking and network topology analysis

• **Subscription & License Management** - Automated tracking and lifecycle 
management of device subscriptions, software licenses, and service entitlements

• **Secure Lifecycle Transitions** - Complete device state management from 
onboarding through operational phases to secure decommissioning with audit trails


**🏢 Enterprise Integration & Scale:**

Built for enterprise environments with seamless integration capabilities,
comprehensive audit trails, high-performance batch processing, and 
enterprise-grade security controls for large-scale network deployments.

- Real-time device discovery with automated classification

- Automated configuration updates and version management

- Integration with asset management and CMDB systems

detection, automated optimization recommendations, intelligent capacity planning

ActionStatusEnum.title: Device Action Status
ActionStatusEnum.description:
Lifecycle state of an asynchronous device action task. Values are the
canonical Common Async Operations states (a subset of the standard set).

State machine:
  PENDING --► RUNNING --► SUCCEEDED
                      L--► FAILED
  ANY     --► CANCELLED

New values may be added in future minor versions; clients MUST handle unrecognised values without error.

| Value | Description   | Terminal |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `PENDING` | Request accepted; the action has not started yet.  | No |
| `RUNNING` | The action is in progress on at least one device.  | No |
| `CANCELLING` | Cancellation has been requested; the action is winding down but has not yet reached a terminal state.  | No |
| `SUCCEEDED` | All targeted devices reached a terminal success state.  | Yes |
| `FAILED` | One or more devices failed (failFast may have short-circuited others).  | Yes |
| `CANCELLED` | The action was cancelled before completion.  | Yes |
| `EXPIRED` | The action was abandoned after its processing deadline (expires_at) without reaching another terminal state.  | Yes |
ActionStatusEnum.x-ai-usage:
Poll until a terminal state is reached (SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED).
On FAILED status, inspect per-device results for error codes and messages.
Implement exponential back-off with a client-side timeout per action type.

Identifies the type of operation to execute on target devices.

This enum is the central registry of all supported device actions.
New action types are introduced by adding a key under actions: in the metadata
YAML and registering a handler — no API contract changes needed.

Planned actions: Additional application lifecycle operations.

New values may be added in future minor versions; clients MUST handle unrecognised values without error.

| Value | Description   | Status |
|-------|-------------|--------|
| `REBOOT` | Restart the device — graceful (NORMAL) or immediate (FORCED).  | Available |
| `ADD_APPLICATION` | Add an application to the application registry on target devices.  | Available |
| `START_APPLICATION` | Start a stopped application on target devices.  | Available |
| `STOP_APPLICATION` | Stop a running application on target devices with graceful or forced mode.  | Available |
| `INSTALL_APPLICATION` | Install an application on target devices from a package source.  | Available |
| `DELETE_APPLICATION` | Delete (uninstall) an application from target devices.  | Available |
| `DEPLOY_APPLICATION` | Deploy an application (install + start) on target devices.  | Available |

DeviceActionRequestVo.title: Device Action Request
DeviceActionRequestVo.description:
Generic request payload for executing any device action (Reboot, Factory Reset, etc.).
The `action_type` field determines the operation to perform.
The optional `device_type` routes the request to the correct handler.
If omitted, the service derives it when the action has a single supported device type.
Action-specific inputs (e.g. reboot_mode) are passed via the `parameters` map.

action_type.description: The action to execute on the target devices.

scope.description: Which devices to act on. Each entry targets either specific devices (DEVICE, by serial number) or a whole site (SITE, by location ID).

device_type.description: Optional. The kind of device to act on (for example UNIVERSAL_COMPUTE_PLATFORM). You can usually leave this out — the service works it out from the devices you target.

scheduled_at.description: Optional. When to run the action, as a UTC date-time (for example 2030-06-01T02:00:00Z). Leave it out to run right away. A time in the past is rejected.

reason.description: Human-readable reason captured in the audit log.

parameters.description:
Action-specific parameter map. Keys and allowed values per action type:

START_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `instance_name` | String[] | Yes |  | Names of the application instances to start |

STOP_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `instance_name` | String[] | Yes |  | Names of the application instances to stop |

INSTALL_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `application_name` | String | Yes |  | Name of the application to install |

DELETE_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `instance_name` | String[] | Yes |  | Names of the application instances to delete |

DEPLOY_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `instance_name` | String[] | Yes |  | Names of the application instances to deploy |

ADD_APPLICATION action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `application_name` | String | Yes |  | Name of the application to add |

REBOOT action parameters:

| Key | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-----|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `reboot_mode` | RebootModeEnum | No | NORMAL | Reboot mode – graceful (NORMAL) or immediate (FORCED). |

instance_name.description: Names of the application instances to start, stop, delete, or deploy.

application_name.description: Name of the application to install or add.

DeviceActionResultVo.title: Per-Device Action Result
DeviceActionResultVo.description: Outcome of an action for a single device within a multi-device request. On initial submission (status = PENDING) contains only deviceId and status. After the action completes, errorCode and errorMessage are populated for failed devices.

device_id.description: The unique numeric device identifier from the device table.

serial_number.description: Device serial number for audit trail and cross-reference.

hostname.description: Device hostname from the system, if available.

status.description: Current status of the action for this specific device.

error_code.description: Machine-readable error code if the action failed for this device.

DeviceActionResponseVo.title: Device Action Response
DeviceActionResponseVo.description:
Response payload for a submitted device action.
On submission (POST /v1/devices:execute-action), status is always PENDING and
device_results contains an initial per-device PENDING entry.
Use task_key to correlate the action; the status URL is returned in the response Location header.

task_key.description: The unique ID for this action. Use it with the status URL (returned in the Location header) to check how the action is progressing.

status.description: Overall task-level status at submission time (always PENDING on 202).

poll_interval_seconds.description: Suggested number of seconds to wait between status polls, matching the Retry-After header value on the initial response.

device_results.description: Per-device result list.  On initial 202 response every entry has status = PENDING.  Final per-device outcomes (SUCCEEDED/FAILED) are available via the polling endpoint once the action completes.

last_updated_at.description: When the most recent per-device status update happened, shown in UTC.

message.description: Human-readable summary message for the overall action.

expires_at.description: The time by which the action must finish. If it has not completed by then, it is given up on. Shown in UTC, for example 2030-06-01T02:10:00Z.

result_expires_at.description: The time after which this action's result can no longer be retrieved. Shown in UTC.

created_at.description: When the action was created and accepted, shown in UTC (for example 2030-06-01T02:00:00Z).

operation_location.description: The URL to check this action's status (the same value as the Location header).

cancel_location.description: The URL to request cancelling this action, when cancelling is supported.

action_type.description: Echo of the original action_type from the request.

device_type.description: Echo of the original device_type from the request.

scheduled_at.description: Scheduled execution time echoed from the request. Null for immediately-executed actions.

X-Trace-ID.description: A unique ID for your request, returned on every response (whether it succeeds or fails). RateLimit.description: How many requests you have left under your current rate limit, and when it resets. Format: "policy-name";r=<remaining>[;t=<seconds-until-reset>]

RateLimit-Policy.description: The rate limit policy that applies to your requests, returned on every response. Limits apply per account or per application — not per individual device. Format: "policy-name";q=<max-requests>;w=<window-in-seconds>

Retry-After.description: Seconds the client should wait before retrying the request. Returned in 429 responses; may also be returned in 503.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Legacy mirror of the rate-limit ceiling for this policy window (transition aid alongside the IETF RateLimit-Policy header; see CRLT-007). Authoritative value is the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` header when the two disagree.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Legacy mirror of how many requests remain in the current window (transition aid alongside the IETF `RateLimit` header; see CRLT-007). Authoritative value is the IETF `RateLimit` header when the two disagree.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Legacy mirror of the number of seconds until the rate-limit window resets (transition aid alongside the IETF `RateLimit` header; see CRLT-007). Always seconds-until-reset — never a Unix timestamp or date.

X-Should-Retry.description: Whether the client should retry this request. `true` indicates transient overload — retry after the duration in Retry-After with backoff. `false` indicates a hard policy violation (e.g. quota exhausted) where retrying is futile until the policy window resets. Disambiguates a bare status code, which cannot express this distinction on its own.
